expected_effect: Fixed 1800 s budget, seed 42, LNC=2 nproc=4: candidate completes +3% to +8% more optimizer steps than the same-host control (about 2135-2240 vs 2071/2076) and finishes with public_val_bpb lower by 0.001 to 0.004 (target <= 1.0047 on trn21, <= 1.0050 on trn22). Falsified if steps are within +/-1% of control (head matmul not a measurable cost) or if steps rise >= 2% but public_val_bpb does not fall by >= 0.001 (BF16 logit rounding costs more than the recovered steps).
hypothesis: At the pinned commit under the controller-fixed environment (NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1', no compiler matmul autocast), the LM-head logits projection [B,T,d] x [d,V] runs as an FP32 matmul on the PE array and is one of the largest single matmuls per token (vocab-sized output; the 55.7M non-table parameters imply the head/embedding matrix is a large fraction of dense FLOPs). Trn2 FP32 matmul throughput is several times lower than BF16. The only KEEP at this commit came from exactly this kind of isolated precision-boundary change (--bf16-sdpa-input: 2233 steps / 1.002028 vs control 2076 / 1.005967 on trn22), and the fresh-start ledger shows BF16 matmul operands are quality-compatible at this scale (0.979-0.993 public BPB under '--auto-cast matmult --auto-cast-type bf16'). Executing only the head matmul with two BF16 operands and immediately upcasting the logits to FP32 (softcap, CE, byte-loss weighting, eval accumulation and causality check unchanged) should raise fixed-budget step count by a few percent with negligible quality loss per step, lowering final public_val_bpb. This concept passed proposal verification twice (r1, r2) and has never been run: r1 failed implementation review for an activation-only cast and missing dtype/parity evidence; r2's implementation review was SKIPPED only because the per-cycle LLM call cap was reached. r3 re-submits the r2 design with the implementation evidence requirements made mandatory and checkable in the smoke log.
implementation_plan: All edits confined to train.py on branch autoloop/20260922-bf16-lm-head-two-operand-r3 from 9a4caa7b. STEP 0 (static check, written to the experiment directory as step0_head_dtypes.md BEFORE any edit): locate the final logits projection -- the F.linear / matmul / (tied) wte-weight product mapping the final-normed hidden state [B,T,d] to vocab logits, immediately upstream of the softcap and cross-entropy (region gated by --nki-softcap-ce and --byte-loss-weight). If the head goes through the project's Linear class, read Linear.forward and its weight-cache code (the same mechanism referenced near train.py lines 3174-3189 / 5251-5266) and record with quoted line ranges: (a) dtype of the activation entering the head call, (b) dtype of the weight tensor actually passed to the matmul (FP32 master vs cached copy) and whether the cache is detached, (c) how gradients reach the FP32 master, (d) whether any torch.autocast context encloses the call, (e) whether --transposed-linear selects a transposed weight mirror at the head, all under default flags (bf16_norm_output False, bf16_sdpa_input False). If both operands are already BF16 or the call is under autocast, stop and return HALT-INERT. STEP 1 (toggle): following the existing --bf16-sdpa-input pattern, add module-level USE_BF16_LM_HEAD = True with env override NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD ('0' disables), argparse pair --bf16-lm-head / --no-bf16-lm-head (dest bf16_lm_head, default None -> constant), and append 'USE_BF16_LM_HEAD' to ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES (or the equivalent list saved into checkpoints and restored by load_for_eval) so the eval/causality path resolves the same value; default must resolve True so the candidate run uses no flags. STEP 2 (boundary): at the logits projection only, when USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is True, execute: h16 = h.to(torch.bfloat16); w16 = head_weight.to(torch.bfloat16) where head_weight is the FP32 master tensor the current code uses (lm_head.weight or tied wte.weight) -- a differentiable .to() cast applied to the master Parameter, NOT a detached weight-cache copy, so autograd accumulates the FP32 master gradient through the cast; logits = F.linear(h16, w16) (or the equivalent matmul form already used; if the transposed-linear layout is active at the head, cast the transposed mirror via the same differentiable .to() and keep the existing layout); logits = logits.float(). If the existing Linear path already casts the weight to BF16 through a custom autograd function that routes gradients to the master, it may be reused only if the activation cast is added and STEP 4 proves both operand dtypes; otherwise bypass it with the direct casts above. Leave every downstream operation (softcap, CE, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation, causality check) untouched so they receive FP32 logits as before. The same forward code serves training and evaluation; no separate eval branch. When USE_BF16_LM_HEAD is False the original call executes unchanged. Do not change tying, create Parameters, or alter initialization, optimizer groups, grad clipping, or any other layer. STEP 3 (logging): add exactly one field 'bf16_lm_head=<bool>' to the existing precision-options config oneliner. STEP 4 (evidence): add a one-time rank-0 log line at the first head call printing the dtypes of the two matmul operands and of the returned logits (guarded by a module-level flag so it prints once); the smoke log must show bfloat16, bfloat16, float32. STEP 5 (verification artifacts for the implementation verifier, all saved in the experiment directory): (a) full diff, limited to the toggle/env/CLI resolution, the ARCH_TOGGLE_NAMES entry, the head-boundary cast block, the one config-log field and the one-time dtype log; (b) grep output showing softcap/CE/byte-loss/eval accumulation code untouched; (c) demonstration that with NEURON_COMPETITION_R1_BF16_LM_HEAD=0 the original call executes (dtype log shows float32, float32, float32 or the log line is absent because the branch is skipped -- state which); (d) quoted checkpoint save and load_for_eval code paths that persist and restore USE_BF16_LM_HEAD; (e) smoke run resolving bf16_lm_head=True, num_params_M 592.9, ngram_ve and oneliners identical to control, causality_passed True, the STEP 4 dtype line, and meeting the smoke gate (>=338 steps, step-rate ratio >=1.01 vs same-host control smoke, public_val_bpb <= control smoke + 0.003). Launch the full run with the exact control launch command and environment (NEURON_LOGICAL_NC_CONFIG=2 torchrun --standalone --nproc_per_node=4 train.py --num-steps 5000 --max-train-seconds 1800 --seed 42, NEURON_CC_FLAGS='--optlevel=1') and no additional flags.
single_causal_change: One numerical-format boundary change confined to train.py: at the LM-head logits projection only, both matmul operands (final-normed hidden activation and the head weight, tied or untied) are temporary BF16 tensors produced by differentiable .to(torch.bfloat16) casts of the FP32 tensors the current code uses; the matmul executes in BF16; the logits are immediately cast .float() so softcap, cross-entropy, byte-loss weighting, eval BPB accumulation and the causality check consume FP32 logits through byte-identical downstream code (values differ only by BF16 rounding of the head matmul). FP32 master parameters, optimizer state, embedding lookup, tying, initialization, all other layers, kernels, schedule, batch, seed, evaluator, launch shape and environment are unchanged; num_params_M must remain 592.9 and the ngram_ve/oneliners must be identical to control. No other precision, kernel, optimizer or architecture switch is touched; no torch.autocast context is introduced. Comparison: same-host pinned control on public_val_bpb (trn21 2071 / 1.005734; trn22 2076 / 1.005967). Outcome classes in order: (1) HALT-INERT if the static check finds both head operands already BF16 (or the call already under autocast) under default flags; (2) CONFOUNDED-SHORT if steps < 90% of same-host control (<1864 trn21, <1869 trn22); (3) FALSIFIED-INERT if steps within +/-1% of control; (4) EXCESS-GAIN-REVIEW if steps > +10% (>2278 trn21, >2283 trn22): compare logged validation trajectories at matched step counts before any quality claim; if unavailable, quality attribution is recorded unresolved; SUCCESS only if public_val_bpb < control by >= 0.001 and no matched-step deficit > 0.010 at the control's final step; (5) SUCCESS if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb < same-host control by >= 0.001; (6) FALSIFIED-QUALITY if steps >= +2% and public_val_bpb >= control; (7) INCONCLUSIVE otherwise.
